question: What liquid solution is standard for preserving a skin biopsy sample on its way to the lab?

options.A: 10% neutral buffered formalin
options.B: Normal sterile saline solution
options.C: Hydrogen peroxide antiseptic
options.D: Isopropyl alcohol 70 percent

explanation: Neutral buffered formalin is the go-to liquid fixative. It stops the tissue from breaking down so the pathologist can examine the cells clearly.

question: Why is psychological rehab just as vital as physical detox when treating substance dependence?

options.A: It replaces the need for any nursing observation or vital sign monitoring
options.B: It ensures the patient never experiences physical withdrawal symptoms again
options.C: It addresses underlying triggers and teaches healthy coping skills to prevent relapse
options.D: It is the only way to restore normal kidney and liver function after drug use

explanation: Brilliant! Detox cleans out the body, but rehab tackles the emotional and behavioral roots of addiction so the patient can learn new ways to cope without drugs.

question: How can chronic (long-term) inflammation lead to a cervical polyp?

options.A: It destroys local nerve endings
options.B: It directly causes malignant cell transformation
options.C: It triggers abnormal tissue proliferation over time
options.D: It blocks the production of estrogen

explanation: Think of it like skin getting a callus from constant friction. Ongoing irritation makes the cervical tissue grow extra cells, forming a polyp over time.

question: You need to find out the exact rate of childhood malnutrition in a rural ward. Where should you check first?

options.A: Local clinic weighing registers and child welfare records
options.B: Folktales told by elderly residents around the evening fire
options.C: Abstract political essays written by national lawmakers
options.D: General gossip gathered at the community market square

explanation: Spot on! Clinic records give you the actual numbers and history on child growth and facility use.

question: Why might relying only on the hospital's liability insurance leave you unprotected as a nurse?

options.A: Institutional coverage automatically pays out cash settlements directly to the nurse
options.B: Hospital attorneys represent the institution and may have interests conflicting with the nurse's
options.C: Employer policies never cover mistakes made during night shifts
options.D: Facility insurance policies expire the moment a nurse takes a short break

explanation: Remember, the hospital's legal team works for the hospital, not you! Their main job is protecting the facility, so having your own backup is smart nursing practice.

question: What is the medicalisation of FGM?

options.A: Using modern local anesthesia during traditional FGM rites
options.B: Performing FGM using trained healthcare workers in clinical settings
options.C: Treating the physical complications of FGM in a hospital
options.D: Researching surgical ways to reverse FGM damage

explanation: Medicalisation refers to health professionals performing the procedure under the false assumption that clinical hygiene removes the harm. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT part of a holistic palliative assessment?

options.A: Respecting cultural beliefs and family traditions
options.B: Strictly monitoring laboratory blood cell counts
options.C: Evaluating emotional and psychological well-being
options.D: Listening to spiritual and existential concerns

explanation: While lab results matter in acute care, palliative care is all about the human experience—feelings, culture, and spirit. It's much more than just numbers on a lab sheet!

question: What is the main danger of having an extremely wide span of control on a busy ward?

options.A: Staff members will have too many layers of bosses to report to
options.B: Communication between departments will completely stop
options.C: Supervision can become stretched too thin, risking safety
options.D: Every nurse will be promoted to a management position

explanation: Spot on! If one nurse manager is trying to oversee too many staff at once, it's easy to miss mistakes and patient safety can suffer.

question: When we talk about 'local sources of nutrients' in Nigerian diets, what do we mainly mean?

options.A: Processed canned foods found in international supermarkets
options.B: Synthetic vitamins manufactured in laboratory settings
options.C: Foods grown and harvested within a community or country
options.D: Expensive dietary supplements imported from overseas

explanation: Spot on! Local nutrient sources are simply the foods naturally grown and produced right here in our environment or nation. It makes eating healthy much more practical!

question: Why can altering a ready-made topical cream cause problems?

options.A: It changes the expiration date to the exact same day
options.B: It breaks down the product stability and preservatives
options.C: It automatically turns the lotion into a liquid
options.D: It causes the active ingredient to evaporate instantly

explanation: Mixing products messes up the chemical balance and can make it easier for bacteria to grow. Don't worry, you'll get the hang of product safety in no time!

question: During a measles outbreak, why do public health teams do 'contact tracing'?

options.A: To collect financial penalties for spreading the infection
options.B: To monitor exposed individuals during the incubation period and offer vaccination
options.C: To test the water supply for bacterial contamination
options.D: To punish individuals who failed to attend the primary health clinic

explanation: Great clinical thinking! Tracing contacts lets nurses catch infections early and vaccinate people before symptoms appear.

question: In nutrition, what does the term DRI stand for?

options.A: Dietary Restriction Index
options.B: Daily Recommended Instructions
options.C: Dietary Reference Intakes
options.D: Daily Routine Intake

explanation: DRIs are just the standard reference values health workers use to check if someone is getting enough nutrients.

question: Why do older adults generally need fewer calories each day compared to younger adults?

options.A: Their digestive systems stop absorbing carbohydrates
options.B: Their basal metabolic rate and physical activity decrease
options.C: They store all their energy directly as water weight
options.D: Their bodies no longer use fat for energy storage

explanation: You got it! As we age, we tend to lose a bit of muscle and move around less, meaning our bodies naturally burn fewer calories overall.

question: What was the main focus of nursing studies during the early part of the twentieth century?

options.A: Hospital staffing and nursing education
options.B: Molecular genetics and cellular biology
options.C: Pharmacological drug trials
options.D: Advanced surgical techniques

explanation: Early research mostly looked at how to organize nursing schools, manage hospital routines, and assign student workloads efficiently. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T3#GNS217_U2_T3_h2)

question: Why must a nurse figure out if a patient's bone or joint problem is an acute injury or a long-term chronic condition?

options.A: Chronic conditions always require immediate emergency surgery
options.B: Chronic conditions cannot be assessed using standard nursing interviews
options.C: Acute injuries never involve any swelling or localized pain
options.D: Acute injuries and chronic conditions require completely different management approaches

explanation: Spot-on! Knowing whether a problem happened suddenly or built up over time completely changes how you care for and manage the patient.

question: What is an important nursing check after a patient has an upper GI scope (endoscopy)?

options.A: Giving strong oral laxatives to clear out remaining dye
options.B: Putting warm compresses on the tummy every 15 minutes
options.C: Checking that the patient's gag reflex is back before giving food or water
options.D: Pushing the patient to eat a heavy meal right away to get their strength back

explanation: The throat spray numbs the back of the throat during the scope. If you feed them before the gag reflex returns, they could easily choke or aspirate.

question: Why should nurses advise patients NEVER to put butter or toothpaste on a fresh burn?

options.A: They cause the top layer of skin to fall off immediately
options.B: These substances trap heat inside the tissue and can introduce bacteria
options.C: They react chemically with sweat to produce dangerous acid
options.D: They neutralize cool tap water and make the wound freeze faster

explanation: Spot on! Kitchen remedies like butter act like a blanket, keeping the heat trapped inside and inviting germs that cause infections.

question: Why does cellular damage occur during prolonged shock?

options.A: Blood vessels expand and physically crush nearby organs
options.B: Cells lack oxygen to produce energy and waste builds up
options.C: Excess water floods the cells and causes them to burst
options.D: White blood cells mistakenly attack healthy body tissue

explanation: Without a steady supply of oxygen, cells cannot make normal energy, causing harmful waste products to accumulate and damage cellular structures. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T2#GNS221_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why is strict confidentiality vital when nursing adolescent patients?

options.A: It builds trust and prevents teenagers from hiding important health details
options.B: It reduces the amount of paperwork nurses must complete daily
options.C: It allows teenagers to prescribe their own medications safely
options.D: It is required by law so parents never have to speak to doctors

explanation: Young people need to know their secrets are safe so they feel secure enough to share honest health concerns. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T4#GNS312_U4_T4_h4)

question: How can a high-protein diet affect a patient who already has chronic kidney disease?

options.A: It replaces the need for routine blood tests
options.B: It has zero impact on their renal system
options.C: It completely cures their kidney disease within weeks
options.D: It can accelerate the decline of their kidney function

explanation: Struggling kidneys find it hard to filter heavy loads of nitrogen waste. For CKD patients, too much protein can actually make their kidney damage worse.

question: How has occupational health nursing changed from the 19th century to the 21st century?

options.A: From working exclusively in hospital wards to running corporate legal departments
options.B: From addressing traumatic physical injuries in heavy factories to managing chronic strain and mental wellness
options.C: From ignoring chemical exposures entirely to treating only rare tropical diseases
options.D: From focusing exclusively on boardroom management to supervising mining operations

explanation: While physical safety is still key, today's occupational nurses focus a lot on ergonomics, mental health, and preventing everyday work stress.

question: What is a common everyday habit that shows bias against people with physical disabilities?

options.A: Mandatory medical quarantine during routine community gatherings
options.B: Strict government laws requiring daily public registration
options.C: Speaking to an accompanying person instead of addressing the individual directly
options.D: Automatic exemption from paying all forms of local utility taxes

explanation: Spot on! Talking to their friend or family member instead of the patient assumes their disability affects their mind, which is a common bias we need to unlearn.

question: What is the most effective public health strategy for preventing obstetric fistulae in communities?

options.A: Improving access to skilled birth attendants and emergency obstetric care
options.B: Administering daily vitamin supplements during the third trimester
options.C: Providing free diapers to all women living in rural communities
options.D: Encouraging women to give birth at home without professional assistance

explanation: You nailed it! Getting help quickly during difficult labour prevents the prolonged pressure that causes fistulas. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h6)

question: Why do many women in Nigeria end up using unsafe abortion methods?

options.A: Strict laws, social stigma, and poor access to safe care
options.B: Surgical facilities are cheap and everywhere
options.C: People just love traditional herbs more than hospitals
options.D: Primary health workers give very clear instructions

explanation: Fear of judgment, legal barriers, and a lack of friendly youth clinics push vulnerable people toward dangerous procedures. Great insight to keep in mind for clinical practice!

question: Who do families in local communities typically trust the most when it comes to health advice?

options.A: Commercial product advertisers
options.B: Nurses and healthcare workers
options.C: Anonymous internet bloggers
options.D: Traveling artifact merchants

explanation: That's you! Nurses hold a special, trusted place in the community, making your health advice powerful for local families.

question: What is the main heart and soul of palliative care nursing?

options.A: Improving quality of life and relieving discomfort for serious illnesses
options.B: Shortening the natural dying process to reduce hospital costs
options.C: Preventing family members from visiting patients in final stages
options.D: Finding a permanent cure for terminal infectious diseases

explanation: Palliative care isn't about curing a disease; it's about wrapping the patient and family in comfort, dignity, and gentle symptom relief.

question: A nurse researcher wants to study patient hygiene habits in a ward without changing their routine. What is the most suitable data collection approach?

options.A: A laboratory test
options.B: A clinical drug trial
options.C: Surgical intervention
options.D: Direct observation

explanation: To see how people naturally behave without them putting on an act, direct observation in their real environment works best. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h4)

question: Why is it important for a nurse to know how different hospital bed accessories work?

options.A: To calculate daily hospital room billing charges
options.B: To train housekeeping staff on proper linen folding
options.C: To select the right tool for a specific patient condition
options.D: To perform routine maintenance on mechanical bed frames

explanation: Brilliant! Knowing how each accessory works allows you to match the correct device to your patient's unique needs and prevent complications. Keep going!

question: At what point should a sharps disposal container be closed and replaced to keep everyone safe?

options.A: One-quarter full
options.B: Halfway full
options.C: Completely filled to the brim
options.D: Three-quarters full

explanation: Never overfill a sharps bin! Closing it when it's three-quarters full ensures protruding needles won't accidentally prick anyone.

question: A clinic is in an area that floods every rainy season. What is the best structural safety step for them?

options.A: Issuing warning pamphlets to patients in the waiting room
options.B: Training nurses on how to swim in fast-moving water
options.C: Buying extra bandages and IV fluids for the pharmacy
options.D: Moving the emergency backup generators to an upper floor

explanation: Brilliant! Elevating power systems protects them from floodwaters so the clinic can keep running.

question: Why is working closely with local and religious leaders so vital for successful immunization drives?

options.A: Village leaders are trained to administer routine injections during staff shortages
options.B: Community members fund the importation of foreign vaccine supplies
options.C: Trusted local voices help address fears and clear up cultural misconceptions about vaccines
options.D: Local leaders inspect refrigerator temperatures every morning before clinic opens

explanation: People trust their community leaders. When elders and local leaders support immunization, families feel safe and eager to bring their children forward!

question: Which lobe of the brain processes the sounds you hear?

options.A: Occipital lobe
options.B: Temporal lobe
options.C: Parietal lobe
options.D: Frontal lobe

explanation: The temporal lobe houses your auditory cortex, turning nerve signals from your ears into clear, recognizable sounds.

question: When is a stool culture typically ordered for a patient with gastroenteritis?

options.A: Only after the patient has fully recovered from illness
options.B: When symptoms are severe, persistent, or contain blood
options.C: To test if the patient's liver enzymes are elevated
options.D: For every single patient who reports mild vomiting

explanation: Routine mild viral cases clear up on their own, so cultures are reserved for severe, prolonged, or bloody presentations to identify the exact germ. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h4)

question: How do fibrin sealants work when you put them on bleeding tissue?

options.A: They numb nerve endings to stop pain
options.B: They permanently dilate local blood vessels
options.C: They lower the local body temperature
options.D: They mimic the final step of the natural clotting process

explanation: Fibrin sealants bring ready-to-use clotting ingredients straight to the wound, acting like a biological glue that creates an instant clot.

question: A patient gets a severe wound infection three days after surgery because the instruments weren't properly sterilized. What is this called?

options.A: An expected medication side effect
options.B: A healthcare-associated infection
options.C: A standard diagnostic failure
options.D: An unavoidable genetic reaction

explanation: Infections that patients pick up while receiving treatment inside a hospital or clinic are known as healthcare-associated infections.

question: Which household practice comes from a misunderstanding about how HIV is spread?

options.A: Refusing to share eating utensils with the patient
options.B: Using separate towels for drying after a bath
options.C: Sleeping in the same room with proper ventilation
options.D: Washing the patient's clothes with regular soap

explanation: You're doing great! HIV is not spread through saliva or by sharing spoons, forks, and cups during meals.

question: Why is good nutrition during early childhood so important?

options.A: Deficits during this window can cause permanent stunting and brain damage
options.B: Young children have fully developed organs that process food slowly
options.C: It prevents the child from ever catching infections later in life
options.D: Children naturally require fewer nutrients than adults do

explanation: Think of early childhood as a critical construction phase. Missing key nutrients here can unfortunately lead to lasting effects on growth and brain development.

question: You want to find out which months malaria cases peak and food is scarcest in a farming village. Which tool should you use?

options.A: A biometric blood test
options.B: A structural house blueprint
options.C: A hospital budget ledger
options.D: A seasonal calendar

explanation: Spot on! Seasonal calendars let you visually map out changes across the year, tracking things like disease cycles and food supply.

question: Which of the following is an example of primary prevention for unintentional injuries among adolescents?

options.A: Prescribing antidepressants after a deliberate self-harm episode
options.B: Providing physical therapy following a severe motor vehicle crash
options.C: Suturing a deep laceration in the emergency treatment room
options.D: Conducting community road safety education and enforcing helmet laws

explanation: Spot on! Primary prevention stops injuries from happening in the first place through safety education, proper rules, and policy enforcement.

question: Which of the following is NOT a good way to ensure a health project is sustainable?

options.A: Involving village leaders in planning from the very beginning
options.B: Relying entirely on foreign staff to make every daily decision
options.C: Using affordable materials available within the local market
options.D: Training local residents as community health volunteers

explanation: Depending completely on outside staff creates dependency and guarantees the project will fail once those outsiders leave. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h6)

question: A public health nurse visits a crowded urban settlement to improve sanitation and teach hygiene. Whose historical footsteps is this nurse following?

options.A: A medieval monk
options.B: A hospital surgical specialist
options.C: An ancient herbalist
options.D: Lillian Wald

explanation: Lillian Wald is a legend in public health! She took nursing straight into busy neighborhoods to tackle health and social needs together.

question: Why do nurses wear masks during sterile procedures like putting in a central line?

options.A: To comply with fire safety codes
options.B: To protect the nurse from inhaling meds
options.C: To stop the nurse's germs from contaminating the sterile field
options.D: To keep their face warm in cold rooms

explanation: Here, the mask protects the patient! It stops your own mouth and nose bacteria from getting into the sterile area.

question: A patient inhales respiratory droplets from a coughing roommate. What link in the chain does the respiratory tract represent for this new patient?

options.A: Reservoir
options.B: Mode of transmission
options.C: Portal of entry
options.D: Infectious agent

explanation: The respiratory tract is the physical pathway through which the pathogen enters the body of the susceptible host. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T95#GNS214_U1_T95_h2)

question: A patient has been on strict bed rest for several weeks. What is likely happening to their bones?

options.A: Calcium storage in the bones is doubling
options.B: Bone-building cells are rapidly making the bones thicker
options.C: Bone breakdown (resorption) is happening faster than bone building
options.D: Spongy bone is turning into solid metal-like columns

explanation: Bones love movement and weight! Without that daily mechanical stress, the bone-builders slow down, letting the breakdown cells take over and weaken the bone density.

question: Why is a full, holistic health assessment important when looking at a gifted child?

options.A: To measure precise intelligence quotients for legal classification
options.B: To ensure the child skips multiple grades in primary school
options.C: To catch hidden issues like underachievement and emotional distress
options.D: To diagnose physical growth abnormalities caused by high intellect

explanation: Brilliant grades can hide a lot of stress! A holistic check helps nurses spot hidden emotional struggles that high intelligence might mask. Keep up the brilliant work!

question: Which of these is NOT a good practice when trying to prevent adverse drug reactions?

options.A: Guessing the patient's weight without asking them
options.B: Checking the patient's allergy history before giving drugs
options.C: Asking about local herbs and supplements
options.D: Following the five rights of medication administration

explanation: Never guess! Drug doses must be exact, especially for vulnerable patients. Always measure or ask for accurate weights.

question: Which of these is NOT a good nursing strategy for helping a patient manage multiple medications?

options.A: Encouraging the use of weekly pillboxes or organizers to track daily doses
options.B: Educating the patient on recognizing early warning signs of adverse drug reactions
options.C: Collaborating with the pharmacist to simplify complicated dosing schedules
options.D: Telling the patient to stop all their medications immediately without consulting the doctor

explanation: Never tell a patient to drop all meds at once! Stopping drugs abruptly can cause dangerous withdrawal or rebound health issues. Changes must always be planned.

question: How does high resistance in the body's blood vessels affect the heart?

options.A: It stops electrical impulses from reaching the lower heart chambers
options.B: It increases afterload, making it harder for the heart to push blood out
options.C: It lowers the heart rate by relaxing the nervous system
options.D: It decreases preload by trapping extra fluid inside the lungs

explanation: When blood vessels are tight, the heart has to work much harder to push blood past them. That extra workload is called afterload!

question: How do voluntary agencies usually work alongside government health services?

options.A: They completely take over ministry duties
options.B: They compete fiercely for patients
options.C: They complement and support public services
options.D: They regulate medical licensing in the country

explanation: Spot on! They don't try to replace government hospitals; instead, they team up to fill gaps and reach people who need help most.

question: What happens when health programs are copied from other regions without a local diagnosis?

options.A: They become cheaper for the local government to maintain
options.B: They automatically succeed because health problems are identical everywhere
options.C: They eliminate all infectious diseases within a single month
options.D: They may fail because they do not fit the local culture or environment

explanation: Every community is unique; interventions that work in one setting can easily fail if applied blindly elsewhere without local data. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h5)

question: Why might a doctor ask for stool samples collected on three different days?

options.A: Stool samples spoil within two minutes of leaving the body.
options.B: Single samples always contain too many confusing bacteria.
options.C: The laboratory requires large volumes of waste for testing.
options.D: Parasites do not release ova in every single bowel movement.

explanation: Worms don't shed eggs constantly, so testing samples over a few days gives the best chance of catching them. Spot on!

question: Which serious brain condition can result from severe oxygen deprivation during labour?

options.A: Hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy
options.B: Neonatal physiological jaundice
options.C: Gestational trophoblastic disease
options.D: Transient tachypnoea of the newborn

explanation: Hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy is brain damage caused by lack of oxygen and blood flow to the brain around the time of birth. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T003#GNS226_U4_T003_h7)

question: Which quality of a study means that if you repeat it, you will get consistent results?

options.A: Reliability
options.B: Neutrality
options.C: Generalizability
options.D: Randomization

explanation: Spot on! Reliability means your tools and methods are dependable and give consistent answers every time.

question: In clinical nursing, what is a 'toxidrome'?

options.A: An antidote given to reverse the effects of a specific snake venom
options.B: A group of signs and symptoms pointing to a specific class of poison
options.C: The physical damage caused by corrosive chemicals on the skin
options.D: The laboratory test used to measure blood alcohol concentration

explanation: Think of a toxidrome as a symptom 'syndrome' caused by a 'toxic' substance. It helps nurses quickly spot what kind of poison is at play!

question: A clinic trains community health workers to give routine vaccines so nurses can focus on complex cases. What is this strategy called?

options.A: Currency devaluation
options.B: Task shifting
options.C: Out-of-pocket billing
options.D: Macroeconomic financing

explanation: Spot on! 'Task shifting' safely passes appropriate duties to trained support staff, helping the healthcare team work smarter and save costs.

question: On day one after a below-knee amputation, what should the nurse do to help prevent joint stiffness (contractures)?

options.A: Encourage the patient to cross their legs while sitting up.
options.B: Limit the time the residual limb rests elevated on pillows.
options.C: Apply a heavy sandbag directly over the end of the stump.
options.D: Keep the residual limb propped up on pillows for the entire day.

explanation: Keeping the stump propped up for too long causes the muscles to tighten in a bent position. We want to keep those joints flexible!

question: An LTC nurse spends a big part of the shift supervising nursing assistants. What is the main reason for this?

options.A: To minimize direct nurse interaction with residents
options.B: To ensure delegated tasks are performed safely and correctly
options.C: To complete administrative paperwork required by the hospital
options.D: To replace the need for formal care planning meetings

explanation: You got it! As the professional nurse, you lead the care team and oversee assistants to make sure daily tasks like hygiene and safety are done properly.

question: In developing areas, which social issue is most tied to high rates of teenage pregnancy?

options.A: Excessive participation in competitive sports
options.B: Poverty and lack of access to education
options.C: High rates of urban migration
options.D: Universal access to family planning clinics

explanation: Correct! Poverty and limited schooling often strip young girls of choices and keep them from knowing about or getting preventive reproductive care.

question: Which of these items should go into the general, non-hazardous waste bin?

options.A: Empty cardboard boxes from IV fluid bottles
options.B: Used disposable injection syringes
options.C: An empty glass vial of chemotherapy drugs
options.D: Gauze soaked with a patient's blood

explanation: Spot on! Clean packaging hasn't touched body fluids or harsh drugs, so it's safe for the general bin. Keep it up! [learn more](GNS122_U5_T2#GNS122_U5_T2_h2)

question: A 55-year-old patient has a 10-year history of poorly controlled high blood pressure. What major condition are they at high risk for?

options.A: Chronic kidney stones
options.B: Cerebrovascular accident
options.C: Iron deficiency anemia
options.D: Degenerative joint disease

explanation: You nailed it! Years of high pressure wear down cerebral blood vessels, putting the patient at high risk for a stroke (cerebrovascular accident).

question: What is a common local complication of improper injection administration?

options.A: Rapid lowering of blood pressure in healthy individuals
options.B: Pain, tissue necrosis, or abscess formation at the site
options.C: Immediate recovery from chronic respiratory illnesses
options.D: Permanent immunity against all forms of bacterial infection

explanation: Poor injection technique or contaminated medication can cause localized tissue damage, pain, and painful abscesses. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T6#GNS122_U4_T6_h6)

question: Which of the following is a fat-soluble vitamin?

options.A: Vitamin A
options.B: Folic acid
options.C: Vitamin C
options.D: Vitamin B12

explanation: Vitamins A, D, E, and K are fat-soluble and can be stored in body fat, unlike the water-soluble B and C vitamins. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T9#GNS215_U6_T9_h2)

question: How soon can a woman theoretically start ovulating again after experiencing an abortion?

options.A: Never until she reaches menopause
options.B: Only after six full months have passed
options.C: Exactly one full year following treatment
options.D: As early as two weeks post-procedure

explanation: Fertility can bounce back remarkably fast after pregnancy termination, which is why birth control counseling must happen immediately during the PAC visit.

question: What is a key role of the nurse when working with community resources for special needs in Nigeria?

options.A: Diagnosing psychiatric disorders without professional consultation
options.B: Passing strict laws to penalize families who hide children at home
options.C: Connecting families to available local support services and reducing stigma
options.D: Building private special education schools using hospital funds

explanation: Nurses serve as advocates and liaisons, helping families find help in their communities while fighting against societal stigma. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T6#GNS324_U4_T6_h8)

question: Which type of exercise is crucial during late recovery to retrain joint awareness and prevent future sprains?

options.A: Passive continuous immobilization
options.B: High-impact sprinting drills
options.C: Heavy weightlifting exercises
options.D: Proprioceptive and balance training

explanation: Balance training teaches the nervous system how to sense where the joint is, protecting it from future missteps. Brilliant way to keep patients injury-free!

question: What is the main goal of gender-transformative nursing care?

options.A: To enforce traditional cultural rules without questioning them
options.B: To eliminate the study of biological sex differences entirely
options.C: To actively challenge harmful stereotypes and promote equality
options.D: To treat all patients using identical physical interventions

explanation: Brilliant! Gender-transformative care means speaking up against unequal power dynamics and harmful norms to help every patient achieve better health.

question: Which nutrient gives the body its fastest and main source of energy?

options.A: Carbohydrates
options.B: Minerals
options.C: Proteins
options.D: Vitamins

explanation: Carbs are our body's favorite quick energy snack! They break down fast into glucose to keep us going through lectures and ward rounds.

question: Which of these is NOT a good idea if you are facing backlash or resistance for your advocacy work?

options.A: Building strong community alliances
options.B: Relying strictly on verified factual data
options.C: Collaborating with professional nursing bodies
options.D: Acting completely alone without informing anyone

explanation: Correct! Trying to fight battles all by yourself puts you at high risk. True safety and strength always come from teamwork and professional support.

question: Why do we need a whole team of different specialists for cancer rehab?

options.A: The physical and emotional needs of survivors are too diverse for one discipline
options.B: It lowers the overall cost of hospital administration
options.C: Hospital rules require multiple signatures for every session
options.D: Doctors are no longer involved in direct patient care

explanation: Cancer touches every part of a person's life, so it takes a collaborative team of different experts to provide truly great care.

question: What is the main purpose of carrier testing in clinical practice?

options.A: To measure the exact physical strength of a newborn baby
options.B: To identify healthy individuals who carry a recessive gene mutation
options.C: To diagnose an advanced degenerative disorder in the elderly
options.D: To cure a genetic disease before it starts showing symptoms

explanation: Carrier testing is designed for people who do not have symptoms themselves but want to know if they could pass a recessive condition to their children. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T20#GNS222_U4_T20_h4)

question: What is the main reason young children experience so many domestic accidents?

options.A: Lack of proper formal education in school
options.B: A deliberate desire to break household rules
options.C: An inherited weakness in motor coordination
options.D: Natural curiosity combined with unsafe surroundings

explanation: Children love to explore their world! When dangerous items are left within their reach, accidents can easily happen.

question: Which specific lobe of the brain houses the primary motor cortex?

options.A: Frontal lobe

question: As a nurse, what is your top priority when assessing someone with suspected food poisoning?

options.A: Measuring chest wall expansion depth

options.C: Evaluating current hydration status
options.D: Testing visual acuity and eye movement

question: Why might a patient with a left atrial myxoma suddenly faint when changing body position?

question: What is the medical term for natural, age-related hearing loss?

options.A: Otosclerosis
options.B: Barotrauma
options.C: Tympanitis
options.D: Presbycusis

explanation: Spot on! Presbycusis is just the natural wear-and-tear on our hearing as we grow older, usually starting with high-pitched sounds.

question: What happens to the glomerular filtration rate (GFR) during a normal pregnancy?

options.C: It drops to near zero

question: What is the main protective job of antioxidants found in fruits and vegetables?

options.A: Neutralizing unstable free radicals that damage cells
options.B: Acting as direct hormones to lower blood pressure

options.D: Providing the main structural foundation for muscle tissue

question: What is a major clinical advantage of barrier methods compared to hormonal contraceptives?

options.A: They provide protection against sexually transmitted infections
options.B: They guarantee a 100 percent prevention rate against pregnancy
options.C: They alter the body's natural hormone levels permanently
options.D: They last for five continuous years without replacement

question: Why is personal protective equipment placed at the very bottom of the control hierarchy?

options.A: It relies on human behavior and fails if the equipment is damaged
options.B: It is always the most expensive option available
options.C: It completely removes the hazard from the environment
options.D: It is the only method that requires worker training

explanation: PPE is considered a last resort because a mistake by the worker or a tear in the gear still leaves them exposed to the danger. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h2)

question: Where does Community-Based Rehabilitation mainly take place?

options.A: A secure psychiatric asylum
options.B: A large federal teaching hospital
options.C: The local community and family home
options.D: A private overseas medical facility

explanation: Spot on! Community-Based Rehabilitation brings care straight to the patient's doorstep, helping them feel right at home with their loved ones and neighbours.

question: Which nursing action is a must when managing a timed suppression test?

question: Which group of people is most vulnerable to problems with temperature regulation?

options.A: Young adults engaging in sports
options.B: Athletes with high muscle mass
options.C: Healthy adults working indoors
options.D: Elderly patients and infants

explanation: Spot on! Babies and older adults have a harder time adjusting to extreme temperatures, so we need to watch out for them.

question: Why is self-medication so common across Nigeria?

options.A: Standard hospitals rarely stock basic pain relief tablets
options.B: People prefer reading package leaflets over talking to doctors
options.C: Hospital queues, costs, and easy access to open-air drug markets drive the practice
options.D: The government mandates that every citizen treat themselves first

explanation: You got it! Long wait times at clinics and financial constraints often push people to easily accessible informal drug vendors instead.

question: Which symptom is most characteristic of thyroid hormone hypersecretion?

options.A: Rapid weight loss and heat intolerance
options.B: Yellowing of the skin and dark urine
options.C: Low blood pressure and extreme fatigue
options.D: Severe weight gain and cold intolerance

explanation: Too much thyroid hormone speeds up the body's metabolism, causing patients to burn energy fast, lose weight, and feel very hot. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T7#GNS211_U1_T7_h3)

question: What is the safest sleeping position to teach parents to prevent SIDS (cot death)?

options.A: On the back (supine position)
options.B: On the stomach (prone position)
options.C: On either side with rolled towels
options.D: Upright in a soft infant seat

explanation: Always back to sleep! Placing babies flat on their backs for naps and bedtime is the safest way to keep their airways clear and lower the risk of SIDS.

question: Why does a cut or break in the skin raise a patient's risk of getting sick?

options.A: Harmful germs can slip straight into the body without any barrier.
options.B: Langerhans cells stop working during healing.
options.C: Skin oil production increases so much that it traps bacteria.
options.D: The skin stops sweating, causing internal organs to overheat.

explanation: Great job! A whole skin barrier blocks germs effortlessly; once that barrier breaks, microbes have an open doorway into deeper tissues. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T3#GNS211_U2_T3_h7)

question: Why must a nurse line up the pressure monitor with the phlebostatic axis before reading blood pressure numbers?

options.A: To keep the electronic monitor screen from turning off
options.B: To prevent false high or false low pressure readings
options.C: To make sure the blood sample does not get contaminated
options.D: To stop the arterial line from forming a blood clot

explanation: Leveling the transducer to the right atrium means gravity won't trick your monitor into giving you fake high or low numbers. Accuracy matters!

question: What does alcohol do to a germ's proteins when you use it for cleaning?

options.A: They multiply rapidly to protect the cell.
options.B: They are denatured and lose their normal shape.
options.C: They dissolve completely into pure water.
options.D: They turn into hard crystals of calcium.

explanation: Brilliant! Alcohol messes up the structure of microbial proteins, making them unfold and clump together, which destroys the germ.

question: How does pharmacokinetic antagonism affect drug levels in a patient's body?

options.A: By binding permanently to every receptor in the nervous system
options.B: By changing the electrical charge of the red blood cells
options.C: By increasing the metabolism or excretion of the other drug
options.D: By stopping the kidneys from producing any urine output

explanation: One drug makes the body break down or flush out the other drug faster, leaving less active medicine floating around. Makes total sense when you break it down!

question: How is Type II FGM different from Type I?

options.A: It also includes removal of the labia minora
options.B: It leaves the clitoris completely untouched

options.D: It is performed exclusively using modern surgical lasers

question: Why is a multidisciplinary team necessary in palliative care?

options.A: To reduce the number of working hours for individual doctors
options.B: Because physical, emotional, and social needs require diverse expert skills
options.C: To ensure that family members never have to help at home
options.D: Because hospital regulations legally mandate large staffing numbers

explanation: It takes a village! Since a serious illness affects the body, mind, and soul, we need different experts—doctors, nurses, social workers, and chaplains—working as a team.

question: What is a major benefit of doing handovers right at the patient's bedside?

options.A: It prevents doctors from ever entering the patient's room
options.B: It completely removes the need for any written nursing notes
options.C: It reduces the total number of required vital sign checks
options.D: It allows patients to hear their care plan and ask questions

explanation: Bedside handovers make patients part of their own healing journey and help catch any mistakes early!

question: You notice a patient's family members have very different ideas about the patient's prognosis. What should you do first?

options.A: Ask the doctor to discharge the patient immediately
options.B: Ignore the disagreement since it doesn't affect physical comfort
options.C: Tell the family that only one person is correct
options.D: Assess each family member separately to understand their unique perspective

explanation: Families cope in different ways and often hold varied beliefs about an illness. Talking to them individually helps you support each person and communicate better. You are doing brilliantly!

question: A child weighs 44 pounds. What is the child's weight in kilograms?

options.D: 88 kg

question: Why do alkaline chemical burns (like lye) often cause deeper tissue damage than acid burns?

options.A: Alkalis cool down the skin cells and stop normal blood circulation

options.C: Acidic solutions cannot pass through the outer layer of fat cells
options.D: Alkalis cause liquefactive necrosis, letting them penetrate deeper into tissue

explanation: Alkalis trigger a process called liquefactive necrosis that dissolves proteins and fats, allowing the chemical to burrow deep into the body.

question: What does the acronym BLS stand for in nursing and emergency care?

options.A: Breathing Lung System
options.B: Body Life Stimulation
options.C: Basic Life Support
options.D: Basic Lung Safety

explanation: BLS stands for Basic Life Support, which covers emergency measures like CPR and AED use. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T6#GNS321_U2_T6_h1)

question: At what exact times after birth is a newborn's Apgar score routinely checked?

options.A: One and five minutes
options.B: Twelve and twenty-four hours
options.C: Ten and twenty minutes
options.D: One and six hours

question: What is a major financial benefit of healthcare sectors sharing their resources?

options.A: Eliminating the need for nursing licensure examinations
options.B: Guaranteeing free healthcare for all private business owners
options.C: Reducing the salaries of medical laboratory scientists
options.D: Preventing the wasteful duplication of expensive equipment

explanation: Sharing costly machines and spaces stops hospitals from wasting money buying the exact same expensive gear that's already nearby.

question: What should you do immediately if you get a needle-stick injury from a used surgical tool?

options.A: Wait until the end of the shift before telling the supervisor

options.C: Report the incident and follow the facility's post-exposure protocol
options.D: Soak the injured finger in strong chemical disinfectant

explanation: Never brush off a sharps injury! Report it right away so you can get quick medical checks and preventive care if needed.

question: Why is it risky for a patient to ignore digestive warning signs like bleeding?

options.A: It permanently damages the teeth due to upward pressure from the gut.

options.C: It will automatically cause the patient to develop severe food allergies.
options.D: It stops the liver from producing essential clotting factors.

explanation: Catching serious issues early is key. Ignoring red flags can mean waiting too long to treat a serious gut problem.

question: Why chat with local community leaders before holding an immunization outreach in their village?

options.A: To ensure the nurse receives financial compensation from the village
options.B: To let the leaders handle the actual administration of injections
options.C: To build trust and reduce resistance or hesitancy among residents
options.D: To bypass government regulations regarding cold chain transport

explanation: Community leaders have the people's ear. Working with them helps families feel safe and excited about getting vaccinated.

question: Why is a fever in a neutropenic patient treated so aggressively?

options.A: It means the cancer has spread to the skin

options.C: Chemotherapy drugs stop working completely if a fever develops
options.D: Fever automatically causes permanent brain damage within minutes

explanation: Without neutrophils, a minor infection can quickly overwhelm the body and cause fatal septic shock, requiring instant antibiotic therapy. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T13#GNS321_U1_T13_h4)

question: Which dressing material comes from seaweed and turns into a soft gel when it meets heavy wound fluid?

options.A: Cotton gauze

options.D: Transparent film

question: What is a single nucleotide polymorphism, often called an SNP?

options.B: An extra chromosome found in inherited disorders
options.C: A tiny alteration in a single building block of DNA
options.D: A complete deletion of an entire human gene

question: Where does the body store extra energy once glycogen reserves are completely full?

question: Which agency is responsible for regulating food and drugs here in Nigeria?

question: What is a nurse leader's best first move when handling a disagreement between community groups?

question: In nursing research, what do we actually mean by 'measurement'?

question: Which of these is a classic example of a physical stressor?

question: Why is data analysis a critical step before planning any healthcare intervention?

question: What main feature sets chronic pain apart from acute pain?

question: Which set of symptoms in a postpartum mother is a strong warning sign of impending eclampsia (seizures)?

question: What sign makes a Type 2 leprosy reaction (ENL) different from a Type 1 reaction?

question: Which of the following structures works closely with the vestibular cortex to maintain posture?

question: Why is it important to warn older adult patients about dizziness while on these drugs?

question: Why are nurses often the very first people to spot victims of gender-based violence?

question: You see blood sugar numbers in a table, but the column header forgot to state the measurement units. What is your best move?

question: What do we mean by 'socioeconomic determinants of health'?

question: What is the main job of bile when it comes to digesting fats?

question: How do DRF exemptions help protect public health in the wider community?

question: What is the main purpose of a soft diet?

question: Which of these is NOT a healthy lifestyle habit for protecting your gut?

question: Which route for measuring body temperature gives the closest reading to core body heat?

question: Why is a patient taking long-term steroid medications at a higher risk of getting infections?

question: What is the primary focus of leadership compared to management in nursing?

question: What is the main difference between atrial fibrillation and a normal sinus rhythm?

question: What physical measurement must be monitored closely when a newborn is suspected of having a subgaleal hemorrhage?

question: What is the main goal of the Drug Revolving Fund (DRF) model in public hospitals?

question: A ward manager wants to change wound care based on one small, poorly designed study. What should the staff nurse do first?

question: Which of these is NOT a typical hurdle when trying to use healthcare audit recommendations?

question: You're a community nurse at a local market. Which activity is a great example of primary prevention for hypertension?

options.B: Distributing free blood pressure medication to people who already have severe stroke symptoms

question: What is a varicocele, which is a known physical cause of male infertility?

question: A patient with yellow fever vomits dark, coffee-ground looking material. What is this classic clinical sign called?

question: What is a vital nursing duty when caring for a pregnant mother with Type III infibulation?

question: Why do nurses give routine immunizations to patients?

question: What is a major risk if someone takes high-dose fat-soluble vitamin supplements for months without a doctor's advice?

question: Why do health organizations strongly oppose 'medicalization'—which is performing FGM in a clinic by trained health workers?

question: How does Hodgkin lymphoma typically spread compared to non-Hodgkin types?

options.A: It only affects organs in the lower belly
options.B: It never spreads outside the bone marrow

options.D: It jumps randomly to distant body parts immediately

question: Why is keeping an eye on chronic health conditions so important during post-abortion care?

options.A: It guarantees immediate fertility restoration
options.B: It prevents minor issues from becoming emergencies
options.C: It eliminates the need for pain medication
options.D: It reduces hospital administrative costs

question: How can an ongoing health condition like diabetes affect a woman's reproductive cycle?

options.A: It prevents the patient from ever taking oral medications
options.B: It completely stops a woman from ever reaching menopause
options.C: It causes immediate permanent vision loss in newborns
options.D: It can throw off hormone balance and lead to irregular periods

question: Why is involving men in family health beneficial for the household?

question: What is the main goal of using disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (DMARDs)?

options.A: To cure bacterial joint infections within a few days
options.B: To replace lost cartilage with artificial tissue instantly
options.C: To lower blood pressure during acute flare-ups
options.D: To slow down long-term immune-mediated joint damage

explanation: DMARDs help calm down an overactive immune system, protecting the joints from long-term, permanent destruction over time.

question: Which member of the palliative team usually helps families navigate money troubles and community resources?

options.A: Social worker
options.B: Pharmacist
options.C: Surgeon
options.D: Physical therapist

explanation: You're right! Palliative social workers are lifesavers when it comes to connecting families with financial aid, support groups, and community resources.

question: What is the main rule for any food or drink included in a fluid diet?

options.B: It must require extensive chewing before swallowing.
options.C: It must be liquid at room or body temperature.
options.D: It must be served exclusively at a warm temperature.

question: What is the best diagnostic test for looking directly at stomach ulcers and taking tiny tissue samples?

options.A: Plain abdominal X-ray
options.B: Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy
options.C: Barium swallow radiography
options.D: Abdominal ultrasound

question: What is the name of the tough, outermost protective layer that wraps around a whole spinal nerve?

options.A: Meninges
options.B: Epineurium
options.C: Perineurium
options.D: Endoneurium

question: Which statement represents objective, professional documentation in a health record?

options.A: Patient states left knee pain is 8 out of 10

options.D: Patient looks lazy and refuses to walk today

explanation: Recording what the patient specifically stated avoids personal bias and maintains professional documentation standards. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h8)

question: What is the main problem in the heart during congestive heart failure?

options.A: The lungs stop producing oxygen for the bloodstream
options.B: The heart rate drops too low to circulate oxygen
options.C: The heart cannot pump blood efficiently to meet body demands
options.D: The valves close too tightly to allow blood flow

explanation: You've got this! Heart failure simply means the heart muscle is too tired or stiff to pump enough blood forward, leading to fluid backup. It's a common condition you'll see often on the wards.

question: Which test is primarily used to collect cellular samples for cervical cancer screening?

options.A: Pelvic ultrasound
options.B: Complete blood count
options.C: Pap smear
options.D: Urinalysis strip

explanation: Correct! A Pap smear gently collects cells from the transformation zone to check for any early, unusual changes.

question: What is the main goal of psychological therapy when caring for someone with a progressive, degenerative illness?

options.A: To reverse the physical damage to brain tissues
options.B: To replace the need for physical and occupational therapy
options.C: To cure the underlying disease process completely
options.D: To help patients and families cope with ongoing changes

question: Why is a neurovascular check critical for a patient wearing a tight plaster cast on their lower leg?

options.A: To determine when the patient is ready to start running exercises
options.B: To detect trapped swelling and poor circulation before permanent nerve or muscle damage occurs
options.C: To check if the patient is allergic to the plaster materials used
options.D: To measure the exact weight of the cast and prevent skin breakdown on the heel

question: A patient with mild arthritis struggles to open childproof medicine caps, so they leave bottles wide open on the table. What is the best nursing advice?

options.A: Advise the patient to use a hammer to break the stubborn plastic caps.
options.B: Take all the medication away and manage it from the nursing office.
options.C: Recommend easy-open non-childproof caps if no young children visit.
options.D: Scold the patient for leaving dangerous chemicals out in the open.

question: Which of these everyday nursing actions is an example of medical asepsis?

options.A: Performing an open surgical operation in the theatre

options.C: Putting on sterile surgical gloves and a gown
options.D: Inserting a urinary catheter using a sterile kit

question: Which nervous system is primarily responsible for the initial physical arousal and increased pelvic blood flow?

question: Why do many patients feel shoulder pain shortly after laparoscopic gallbladder surgery?

options.B: Muscle strain from lifting heavy things too early

options.A: Celiac sprue

options.A: Young adults with desk jobs

question: Why might you still need to watch a patient with a normal blood pressure for poor circulation?

options.A: Blood pressure is the least important vital sign in critical care

options.D: Normal blood pressure guarantees the heart is pumping perfectly

explanation: The body is smart—it can tighten blood vessels to keep numbers looking normal for a while, even when tissues are starving for oxygen.

question: An 80-year-old patient with mild nerve numbness in their hands (neuropathy) is going home. Which safety change is most important?

question: What kind of thinking or belief is a classic sign of a patient with GPI?
